events.title: Surveyor 1 Achieves First U.S. Soft Lunar Landing
events.summary: Touchdown in Oceanus Procellarum confirmed lunar soil could safely support heavy crewed Apollo landers and returned 11,240 surface photographs.

events.title: Surveyor 3 Lands Inside Shallow Lunar Crater
events.summary: Deployed a robotic surface sampler arm to dig trenches and test regolith mechanics before ceasing transmissions on May 3, 1967.

events.title: Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage Remains at Tranquility Base
events.summary: Following the first crewed lunar landing, the Eagle descent stage served as the launch pad for the ascent stage and became humanity's first crewed hardware left on the Moon.

events.title: Apollo 12 Crew Revisits Surveyor 3 & Deploys First ALSEP
events.summary: Astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked into Surveyor Crater to retrieve Surveyor 3's TV camera and scoop, while activating the first nuclear-powered ALSEP geophysical array.

events.title: First Lunar Roving Vehicle Drives Across Hadley-Apennine
events.summary: LRV-1 expanded astronaut traverse range to 27.8 km around Hadley Rille before being parked permanently near the Falcon descent stage.

events.title: Apollo 17 Concludes Apollo Surface Hardware Deployments
events.summary: Challenger descent stage, LRV-3 (35.9 km driven), and the final ALSEP station were left at Taurus-Littrow Valley.

events.title: Viking 1 Lander Touches Down at Chryse Planitia
events.summary: Delivered the first long-duration surface laboratory and panoramic camera photographs from the surface of Mars.

events.title: Viking 2 Lander Begins Operations on Utopia Planitia
events.summary: Operated on the northern Martian plains, recording winter water-ice frost and seismic monitoring data.

events.title: NASA Switches Off Apollo ALSEP Network
events.summary: After nearly eight years of lunar seismic and magnetic monitoring, operating ALSEP stations were commanded off due to budget constraints.

events.title: Viking 2 Lander Ceases Operations on Utopia Planitia
events.summary: After 1,281 sols of Martian surface weather and frost observations, Viking 2 stopped transmitting when its batteries failed.

events.title: Final Contact with Viking 1 Lander After 2,245 Sols
events.summary: An erroneous uplink command caused the lander's antenna to point away from Earth, ending over six Earth years of Martian operations (mission ended November 13, 1982).

events.title: Mars Pathfinder Lands & Sojourner Becomes First Mars Rover
events.summary: Pathfinder landed on July 4 and Sojourner rolled onto Ares Vallis on July 6, operating for 83 sols before contact ended on September 27, 1997.

events.title: Twin Rovers Spirit and Opportunity Land on Opposite Sides of Mars
events.summary: Spirit (Gusev Crater) and Opportunity (Meridiani Planum) began landmark geologic expeditions that far exceeded their 90-sol plans.

events.title: Spirit Sends Final Transmission from Gusev Crater
events.summary: Immobilized in soft sand at Troy, Spirit fell silent during Martian winter after 7.73 km of driving; NASA concluded recovery efforts on May 25, 2011.

events.title: Opportunity Mission Concludes After 45.16 km Traverse
events.summary: Following a planet-encircling dust storm on June 10, 2018 that blocked solar power, NASA formally concluded Opportunity's 5,111-sol mission.
